questions.q: Suppose $f: R \to \left($0, $\infty\right)be a differentiable function such that 5f\left($x + y\right) = $f\left($x\right)\cdotf  \left($y\right), \forall  x, y \in R$, If f\left($3\right) = 320$, then $\mathop{∑}_{n = 0}$^{5}f\left($n\right) is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given, equation is:

$5f \left(x + y\right) = f \left($x\right)$\cdotf \left(y\right) . . . \left(1\right)$

At~$x = 0, y = 0$, we get

$5f \left(0\right) = f \left($0\right)2 ⇒ f \left(0\right) = 5$

Put~$y = 1$~in~\left(1\right)$, then we get

$5f \left($x + 1\right) = f \left($x\right)\cdotf\left(1\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{f\left(x + 1\right)}{f\left(x\right)} = \dfrac{f\left(1\right)}{5}$

$⇒ \dfrac{f\left(1\right)}{f\left(0\right)} \cdot \dfrac{f\left(2\right)}{f \left(1\right)}\cdot \dfrac{f \left(3\r$right)}{f\left($2\right)} = $\left(\dfrac{f\left(1\right)}{5}\right)$3$

$⇒ $\dfrac{320}{5} = \dfrac{\left(f \left(1\right)\right)3}{53}$⇒ f \left(1\right) = 20$

$∴ 5f\left(x + 1\right) = 20 $\$cdotf\left(x\right)$

$⇒ f \left(x + 1\right) = 4f \left($x\right)$

So,

f\left($1\right) = $4f\left($0\right) = 4 $\cdot5f\left($2\right) = $4f\left($1\right) = {4}^{2} $\cdot5f\left($3\right) = $4f\left($2\right) = {4}^{3} $\cdot5f\left($4\right) = $4f\left($3\right) = {4}^{4} $\cdot5f\left($5\right) = $4f\left($4\right) = {4}^{5} $\cdot$5$

$\mathop{∑}_{n = $0}^{5}f\left($n\right) = 5 + 5 $\cdot$4 + 5 $\cdot {4}^{2} +$5 $\cdot {4}^{3} +$5 $\cdot {4}^{4} +$5 $\cdot {4}^{5}

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{n = $0}^{5}f\left($n\right) = \dfrac{5\left({4}^{6} - 1\right)}{3} =6825$

$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & f(x)=\frac{2^x}{2^x+\sqrt{2}} \\ & f(x)+f(1-x)=\frac{2^x}{2^x+\sqrt{2}}+\frac{2^{1-x}}{2^{1-x}+\sqrt{2}} \\ & =\frac{2^x}{2^x+\sqrt{2}}+\frac{2}{2+\sqrt{2} 2^x}=\frac{2^x+\sqrt{2}}{2^x+\sqrt{2}}=1\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & \text { Now, } \sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{81} \mathrm{f}\left(\frac{\mathrm{k}}{82}\right)=\mathrm{f}\left(\frac{1}{82}\right)+\mathrm{f}\left(\frac{2}{82}\right)+\ldots \ldots+\mathrm{f}\left(\frac{81}{82}\right) \\ & =\mathrm{f}\left(\frac{1}{82}\right)+\mathrm{f}\left(\frac{1}{82}\right)+\ldots \ldots+\mathrm{f}\left(1-\frac{2}{82}\right)+\mathrm{f}\left(1-\frac{1}{82}\right)\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & {\left[\mathrm{f}\left(\frac{1}{82}\right)+\mathrm{f}\left(1-\frac{1}{82}\right)\right]+\left[\mathrm{f}\left(\frac{2}{82}\right)+\mathrm{f}\left(1-\frac{2}{82}\right)\right]+\ldots .40 \text { cases }+\mathrm{f}\left(\frac{41}{82}\right)} \\ & (1+1+\ldots .+1) 40 \text { times }+\frac{2^{1 / 2}}{2^{1 / 2}+2^{1 / 2}} \\ & 40+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{81}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let  \left[x\right]$ denote the greatest integer less than or equal to $x .$~Then, the values of $x \in R$ satisfying the equation \left[e^{x}\right]2 + \left[e^{x} + 1\right] - 3 = 0& lie in the interval:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given equation is& \left[e^{x}\right]2 + \left[e^{x} + 1\right] - 3 = 0$

We know that~\left[x + I\right] = \left[x\right] + I, I \in Z,$~where~\left[\cdot\right],$~represents the greatest integer function.

$⇒ \left[e^{x}\right]2 + \left[e^{x}\right] + 1 - 3 = 0$

Let,~\left[e^{x}\right] = t$

$⇒ t^{2} + t - 2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(t + 2\right)\left(t - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ t = - 2, 1$

But~\left[e^{x}\right] = - 2,$~$($Not possible because we know that $e^{x} > 0 )$

Hence,~\left[e^{x}\right] = 1$~and also, we know that if~\left[x\right] = 1, ⇒ 1 \le x < 2$

$∴ 1 \le e^{x} < 2$

And,~now~by using the definition of logarithm, we have,~if~$e^{x} = a,$~then~$\log_{\mathrm{e}}a = x$

$⇒ \log_{\mathrm{e}}1 \le x < \log_{\mathrm{e}}2$

$⇒ 0 \le x < \log_{\mathrm{e}}2$

$⇒ x \in \left[0, \log_{\mathrm{e}}2\right) .$

$

questions.q: The total number of functions,& $f: \left\{1, 2, 3, 4\right\} \to  \left\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\right\}$~such that $f\left(1\right) + f\left(2\right) = f\left(3\right), is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $f \left(1\right) + f \left($2\right) = f \left(3\right)$

Now possible values of $f \left(3\right)$ are $2, 3, 4, 5$~and $6$~(it cannot be $1$~as minimum value $f \left(1\right) \text{ and } f \left($2\right)$~is~$1$, so~$1 + 1 = 2$~)

For each $k$, if $f \left($3\right) = k$ then there will be \left($k - 1\right)$ set of values for $f \left($1\right)$ and $f \left($2\right)$

For example if $f \left(3\right) = 3$~then possible value of~$f\left(1\right) \text{ and } f\left(2\right)$~will be~\left(1, 2\right)\text{or}\left(2, 1\right) ⇒$~$2$~values~

Similarly for~$f\left(3\right) = 4$,~possible values will be~\left(1, 3\right), \left(3, 1\right), \left(2, 2\right) ⇒3$~values.

And so on.

So number of possible combinations of $f \left(1\right), f \left($2\right)$ and $f \left(3\right)$ are $1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15$

And for each value of~$f \left(3\right)$~there will be~$6$~possible value of~$f \left($4\right)$, so total cases will be~$15 \times6 = 90$

$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& f(x)+2 f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)=x^2+5 \\ & f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)+2 f(x)=\frac{1}{x^2}+5 \\ & f(x)=\frac{2}{3 x^2}-\frac{x^2}{3}+\frac{5}{3} \\ & \alpha=\int_1^2\left(\frac{2}{3 x^2}-\frac{x^2}{3}+\frac{5}{3}\right) \mathrm{dx} \\ & \left(-\frac{2}{3 x}-\frac{x^3}{9}+\frac{5 x}{3}\right)_1^2 \\ & -\frac{1}{3}-\frac{8}{9}+\frac{10}{3}+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{9}-\frac{5}{3} \\ & \alpha=2-\frac{7}{9}=\frac{11}{9} \\ & 2 g(x)-3 g\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=x \\ & \mathrm{~g}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=-\frac{1}{2} \\ & \mathrm{~g}(\mathrm{x})=\frac{\mathrm{x}}{2}-\frac{3}{4} \\ & \beta=\int_1^2\left(\frac{x}{2}-\frac{3}{4}\right) d x \\ & \left(\frac{x^2}{4}-\frac{3 x}{4}\right)_1^2=1-\frac{3}{2}-\frac{1}{4}+\frac{3}{4}=0 \\ & 9 \alpha+\beta=11 \\ & \text { option (4) }
\end{aligned}$

$⇒ f\left(g\left(x\right)\right) = \left\{$\begin{array}{ll}2 + 2\left|x\right|, \left|x\right| \in [ - 1, 0 ) ⇒ x \in ϕ \\ 1 - \dfrac{\left|x\right|}{3}, \left|x\right| \in \left[0, 3\right]\end{array}$\right

$\left\{\text{as}x \in \left[- 3, 3\right]\text{for}\left|x\right| \le 3\text{but}x \in \left[- 3, 1\right]\text{in}g\left(x\right)\right\}$

$⇒ f\left(g\left(x\right)\right) = 1 - \dfrac{\left|x\right|}{3}, x \in \left[- 3, 1\right]$

Now, maximum value of $f\left(g\left(x\right)\right) = 1 - \dfrac{\left|x\right|}{3} = 1 - \dfrac{0}{3} = 1$

$⇒ f\left(g\left(x\right)\right) = \left\{$\begin{array}{ll}2 + 2\left|x\right|, \left|x\right| \in [ - 1, 0 ) ⇒ x \in ϕ \\ 1 - \dfrac{\left|x\right|}{3}, \left|x\right| \in \left[0, 3\right]\end{array}$\right

$\left\{\text{as}x \in \left[- 3, 3\right]\text{for}\left|x\right| \le 3\text{but}x \in \left[- 3, 1\right]\text{in}g\left(x\right)\right\}$

$⇒ f\left(g\left(x\right)\right) = 1 - \dfrac{\left|x\right|}{3}, x \in \left[- 3, 1\right]$

Now, maximum value of $f\left(g\left(x\right)\right) = 1 - \dfrac{\left|x\right|}{3} = 1 - \dfrac{0}{3} = 1$ 

And minimum value is given by $f\left(g\left(x\right)\right) = 1 - \dfrac{3}{3} = 1 - 1 = 0$

Hence, the range of the function will be $\left[0, 1\right]$

questions.q: The number of bijective function $f \left(1, 3, 5, 7, ⋯ , 99\right) \to  \left($2, 4, 6, 8, ⋯ , 100\right)$ if $f  \left($3\right) > f \left($5\right) > f \left(7\right) ⋯ > f\left(99\right)$ is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $f \left(1, 3, 5, 7, ⋯ , 99\right) \to \left($2, 4, 6, 8, ⋯ , 100\right)$

The number of elements in domain and codomain is~$99$.

Now, let us assume~f\left($1\right) = 100$

Now as per diagram we have only~$1$~way for arranging~$f \left($3\right) > f \left($5\right) > f \left(7\right) ⋯ > f\left(99\right)$,

Similarly if we choose~$f\left(1\right) = 98$~then again we have only~$1$~way for arranging $f \left(3\right) > f \left(5\right) > f \left(7\right) ⋯ > f\left(99\right)$,

So we can see the arrangement~$f \left(3\right) > f \left($5\right) > f \left(7\right) ⋯ > f\left(99\right)$~depends upon~$f \left($1\right)$,

So number of ways for choosing~$f \left($1\right)$~is~$C1 50$

questions.q: & If $f ( x + y ) = f ( x ) f ( y )$ and $\mathop{Σ}_{x = 1}^{∞}f\left(x\right) = 2, x, y \in N$, where $N$ is the set of all natural numbers, then the value of $\dfrac{f ( 4 )}{f ( 2 )}$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f ( x ) = a^{x}$~satisfies the functional relation, so
$\mathop{Σ}_{x = 1}^{∞}f\left(x\right) = 2$
$⇒ a + a^{2} + a^{3} \ldots \ldots \infty \text{terms} = 2$
$⇒ \dfrac{a}{1 - a} = 2$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{2}{3}$
$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)x$
Now, $\dfrac{f ( 4 )}{f ( 2 )} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)4}{\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)2} = \dfrac{4}{9}$

questions.q: Let the domain of the function& $f \left(x\right) = \log_{4}  \left(\log_{5}\left(\log_{3}\left($18x - x^{2} - 77\right)\right)\right)$~be~  \left(a, b\right)$.~Then the value of the integral~${∫}_a^{b}\sin^{3}x  \left(\sin^{3}x + \sin^{3} \left($a + b - x\right)\right)$& is equal to _____.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
For domain& $\log_{5}\left(\log_{3}\left(18x - x^{2} - 77\right)\right) > 0$

$\log_{3}\left(18x - x^{2} - 77\right) > 1$

$⇒ 18x - x^{2} - 77 > 3$

$⇒ x^{2} - 18x + 80 < 0$

$⇒ x \in \left(8, 10\right)$

$⇒ a = 8$~and~$b = 10$

$I = {∫}_a^{b}\dfrac{\sin^{3}x}{\sin^{3}x + \sin^{3}\left(a + b - x\right)}$dx$

Apply~${∫}_a^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_a^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right)dx$

$I = {∫}_a^{b}\dfrac{\sin^{3}\left(a + b - x\right)}{\sin^{3}x + \sin^{3} \left(a + b - x\right)}$dx$

$⇒ 2I = \left($b - a\right) ⇒ I = \dfrac{b - a}{2}\left(∵ a = 8 \text{ and } b = 10\right)$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{10 - 8}{2} =1$

$

questions.q:
Let& $f^{1} \left($x\right) = $\dfrac{3x + 2}{2x + 3},$x \in \mathbb{R} - \left\{- \dfrac{3}{2}\right\}$. For $n ≥ 2$, define $f^{n}\left(x\right) = f^{1}of^{n - 1}\left(x\right)$. If $f^{5}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{ax + b}{bx + a},\gcd \left(a, b\right) = 1$, then $a + b$ is equal to ________

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$f^{1} \left(x\right) = $\dfrac{3x + 2}{2x + 3}

Now,

$f^{2}\left(x\right) = f^{1}of^{1}\left(x\right)$

$⇒ f^{2}\left(x\right) = $\dfrac{3\left(\dfrac{3x + 2}{2x + 3}\right) + 2}{2\left(\dfrac{3x + 2}{2x + 3}\right) + 3}

$⇒ f^{2}\left(x\right) = $\dfrac{9x + 6 + 4x + 6}{6x + 4 + 6x + 9}

$⇒ f^{2} ( x ) = $\dfrac{13x + 12}{12x + 13}

$⇒ f^{3}\left(x\right) = $\dfrac{3\left(\dfrac{13x + 12}{12x + 13}\right) + 2}{2\left(\dfrac{13x + 12}{12x + 13}\right) + 3}

$⇒ f^{3}\left(x\right) = $\dfrac{63x + 62}{62x + 63}

$⇒ f^{4}\left(x\right) = $\dfrac{3\left(\dfrac{63x + 62}{62x + 63}\right) + 2}{2\left(\dfrac{63x + 62}{62x + 63}\right) + 3}

$⇒ f^{4}\left(x\right) = $\dfrac{313x + 312}{312x + 313}

$∴ f^{5}\left(x\right) = $\dfrac{1563x + 1562}{1562x + 1563} = \dfrac{ax + b}{bx + a}

$∴ a + b = 1563 + 1562 = 3125

$

questions.q: Let $A = { 1, 2, 3, \ldots . 7 }$ and let $P ( A )$denote the power set of $A$. If the number of functions $f: A \to P ( A )$ such that $a \in f ( a ) , \forall  a \in A$ is $m^{n}, m$ and $n \in N$ and $m$ is least, then $m + n$ is equal to ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$A = { 1, 2, 3, \ldots . 7 }$

And $f: A \to P ( A )$ and $a \in A$

Also $a \in f ( a )$, that means $‘ a ’$ will be the element of subset as $f: A \to P ( A )$,

Now, total options for $1$ will be ${2}^{6}$. (Because ${2}^{6}$ subsets contains elements$1$)

Similarly, for every other element we get, total ${2}^{6} \times {2}^{6} \times {2}^{6} \times {2}^{6} \times {2}^{6} \times {2}^{6} \times {2}^{6} = {2}^{42}$ subsets.

Now, comparing with $m^{n}$ we get, $m = 2 & n = 42$

Hence, $m + n = 2 + 42 = 44$

questions.q: Let $c, k \in R$. If $f\left(x\right) = \left(c + 1\right)x^{2} + \left(1 - c^{2}\right)x + 2k$~and $f\left(x + y\right) = f\left(x\right) + f\left(y\right) - xy$, for all $x, y \in R$, then the value of \left|2\left(f\left(1\right) + f\left(2\right) + f\left(3\right) + \ldots \ldots + f\left(20\right)\right)\right|$ \text{ and } is equal to ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $f \left(x\right) = \left($c + 1\right)x^{2} + \left($1 - c^{2}\right)x + 2k ⋯ \left($i\right)$

&~f\left($x + y\right) = $f\left($x\right) + $f\left($y\right) - xy \forall xy \in R$

So~$f^{'}\left($x\right) = $2\left($c + 1\right)x + 1 - c^{2}$

Now~$\lim_{y \to 0}$\d$dfrac{f\left(x + y\right) - f\left(x\right)}{y} = \lim_{y \to 0}$\dfrac{f\left(y\right) - xy}{y} = \lim_{y \to $0}\dfrac{f\left(y\right)}{y} -$x$

$⇒ f^{'}\left($x\right) = f^{'}\left($0\right) - x$

Integrating, we get

f\left($x\right) = - \dfrac{x2}{2} +f^{'}\left($0\right)x + \lambda$~but~f\left($0\right) = 0 ⇒ \lambda = 0$

i.e.~$f \left($x\right) = - \dfrac{x2}{2} +\left(1 - c^{2}\right)x ⋯ \left($ii\right)$

$∴$~ as~$f^{'} \left(0\right) = 1 - c^{2}$

Now comparing equation~\left(i\right)$~and~ \left($ii\right)$, we get

$c = - \dfrac{3}{2}$

$∴ f\left($x\right) = - \dfrac{1}{2}x^{2} - \dfrac{5}{4}x$

Now~\left|$2\mathop{∑}_{x = 1}^{20}f\left($x\right)\right| = \mathop{∑}_{x = 1}^{20}x^{2} + \dfrac{5}{2} \cdot \mathop{∑}_{x = 1}^{20}x = \dfrac{20 \left(21\right) \left(41\right)}{6} + \dfrac{5}{2} \left(\dfrac{20\left(21\right)}{2}\right)$

$= 2870 + 525$

$= 3395$

$

questions.q: For some $a, b, c \in \mathbb{N}$, let $f\left(x\right) = ax - 3$~and $g\left(x\right) = x^{b} + c, x \in \mathbb{R}$. If \left(fog\right)- 1\left(x\right) = \left(\dfrac{x - 7}{2}\right)\dfrac{1}{3},then~  \left(f ∘ g\right)\left(ac\right) + \left(g ∘ f\right)\left(b\right)$ is equal to _____ .$$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$f\left(x\right) = ax - 3$~

$g\left(x\right) = x^{b} + c, x \in \mathbb{R}$~\left(fog\right)- 1\left(x\right) = $\left(\dfrac{x - 7}{2})\dfrac{1}{3}

Now, let

$h\left(x\right) = \left(f ∘ g\right) \left($x\right)$

$⇒ h^{- 1}$\left($x\right) = $\left(\dfrac{x - 7}{2})\dfrac{1}{3}$

Let

$y = \left(\dfrac{x - 7}{2}\right)\dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ y^{3} = \left(\dfrac{x - 7}{2})

$⇒ x = 2y^{3} + 7$

So, inverse of~$h^{- 1} \left(x\right)$~is~$2x^{3} + 7$~i.e.,~

$h\left(x\right) = fog\left(x\right) = 2x^{3} + 7$

Also,

$fog\left(x\right) = a\left(x^{b} + c\right) - 3$

$⇒ ax^{b} + ac - 3 = 2x^{3} + 7$

On comparing, we get

$a = 2, b = 3, c = 5$

So,

$f\left(x\right) = 2x - 3g\left(x\right) = x^{3} + 5$

Now,

$fog\left(ac\right) = fog\left(10\right) = f\left(1005\right) = 2007$

\left(gof\right)\left(b\right) = gof\left(3\right) = g\left(3\right) = 32$

Therefore,

$fog\left(ac\right) + \left(gof\right)\left($b\right) = 2007 + 32 = 2039$
